title: Dynamics 365 Contact Center: Service Operations Agent for conversational admin setup
summary: The roadmap facts, billing controls and documented agent capabilities are supported. Minor corrections remain: cite the overview behind the configuration-change description and acknowledge the checklist controls missing from the controls table. The earlier HTTP 429 findings did not recur.

claims.claim: Service Operations Agent is an administrator-facing conversational AI for configuration, validation and troubleshooting in Dynamics 365 Contact Center.
claims.quote: Service Operations Agent in Dynamics 365 Contact Center is a self-service AI agent that supports administrators with configuration, validation, and troubleshooting tasks.

claims.claim: It supports conversational setup of Dataverse tables including queues and workstreams.
claims.quote: Service Operations Agent supports conversational setup of Dataverse tables, such as queues and workstreams.

claims.claim: It helps set up channels and workstreams.
claims.quote: Help set up channels and workstreams.

claims.claim: It synchronises phone numbers with Azure Communication Services and Teams.
claims.quote: Sync phone numbers with Azure Communication Services and Teams.

claims.claim: It creates queues with out-of-the-box assignment methods.
claims.quote: Create a queue with one of the out-of-the-box assignment methods.

claims.claim: It adds users to queues.
claims.quote: Assign users to specific queues.

claims.claim: It creates skills.
claims.quote: Create skills and assign them to users.

claims.claim: It sets up operating hours.
claims.quote: Set up operating hours.

claims.claim: It manages capacity profiles.
claims.quote: Create a capacity profile with default max units, reset duration, and block-assignment settings.

claims.claim: It answers questions about the environment and supplies diagnostics for supported channels.
claims.quote:
Ask questions about the environment.
- Provide diagnostics for supported channels.

claims.claim: It creates workstreams and route-to-queue rules without conditions.
claims.quote:
Use natural language instructions to create workstreams and route-to-queue rules.

- You can create multiple rules, but without conditions only.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft describes conversational setup as keeping a human in the loop.
claims.quote: Use natural language to set up your contact center and watch Service Operations Agent run the steps while keeping a human in the loop.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The agent can present draft actions for administrator review and confirmation.
claims.quote: Depending on the scenario, it may also retrieve relevant configuration information, guide users through multi-step tasks, or present draft actions for administrator review and confirmation.

claims.claim: The agent is not designed to operate as an autonomous system.
claims.quote: It supports administrators within the product experience and isn't designed to replace administrator judgment or operate as an autonomous system.

claims.claim: Multistep setup and troubleshooting varied more in testing and may need clarification.
claims.quote: multistep setup and troubleshooting scenarios showed more variability and might require additional clarification or confirmation.

claims.claim: Ambiguous prompts can produce incorrect or incomplete results.
claims.quote: Service Operations Agent might provide incomplete guidance, request clarification, or return incorrect or partial results when prompts are ambiguous

claims.claim: The workstream and queue must be for the same channel.
claims.quote: Make sure that the workstream and queue are for the same channel.

claims.claim: Microsoft advises clear prompts with relevant channel and configuration names.
claims.quote: Use clear, detailed prompts, and explicitly specify the relevant channel or topic to reduce the risk of inaccurate or unreliable answers.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends verifying configuration outcomes in the admin experience, particularly in production.
claims.quote: Organizations should maintain review and verification steps for setup and configuration changes, particularly in production environments

claims.claim: Pay-as-you-go setup links an Azure subscription to a Power Platform environment.
claims.quote: To set up pay-as-you-go billing, you first need an active Azure subscription. Then, you link the subscription to your Power Platform environment

claims.quote: For pay-as-you-go, use Microsoft Cost Management in the Azure portal to view detailed usage and adjust spending limits (budgets) to free up more capacity.

claims.claim: Pay-as-you-go is available for production and sandbox environments.
claims.quote: Pay-as-you-go is available for production and sandbox environments.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Azure meters for Power Platform are billed to the billing plan's Power Platform account resource.
claims.quote: When a billing plan is created, a corresponding Power Platform account resource is created in the Azure subscription that's specified by the billing plan. All Azure meters for Power Platform products are billed to this resource.

claims.claim: The connected Application Insights resource can incur additional Azure ingestion and retention charges.
claims.quote: Because workspace-based Application Insights resources store their data in a Log Analytics workspace, the billing for data ingestion and retention is done by the workspace where the Application Insights data is located.

claims.claim: Removing an environment from its billing policy stops further pay-as-you-go charges for that environment.
claims.quote: As soon as you take either action above, the environment ceases to be pay-as-you-go and goes back to functioning as a regular environment. Any usage that was already incurred up to this point is billed to your Azure subscription, but no further usage is charged.
